notes: Split in November 2026 out of the single IN-HIMALAYA pack (134 species) into three packs, west, Sikkim and Ladakh, so a bird sits in exactly one of them; birds that live in both the western and the eastern Himalaya (Kalij Pheasant, Spotted Forktail, Red-billed Leiothrix, Rufous Sibia, Crimson Sunbird and more) were put in the pack where a visitor most often meets them, and are for the owner to settle. Ladakh and the high Himalaya above the tree line (Leh, Hemis, Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri, Spiti): snowcocks, plateau larks, snowfinches, cliff birds and raptors, rivers and marsh birds. Wide-ranging high mountain birds (Lammergeier, Golden Eagle, choughs, Snow Pigeon, Chukar, Himalayan Snowcock) are kept here on purpose so that each bird sits in exactly one pack. Pallas's Fish-Eagle is here for the lakes of the plateau. Notes of the original Himalaya pack, which still apply to the photos: Hand-picked birds of the Himalaya and its foothills that the India trip does not have: the oak, rhododendron and conifer forests of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh (Corbett foothills, Nainital, Binsar, Mussoorie, Chopta, Great Himalayan NP, Dharamshala, Kullu), the hill forests of Darjeeling and Sikkim (Singalila, Lava, Yumthang) and the high dry plateau of Ladakh. Picked from the country's species with GBIF/eBird counts (in/occurrence.csv, whole India) as a ranking signal plus birding knowledge; vagrants, expedition-only birds and species that are rarely seen even by dedicated birders are out (Western Tragopan, Snow Partridge, Cheer Pheasant, Hill Partridge, Himalayan Owl, Mountain Scops Owl, most Eastern Himalaya wren-babblers and parrotbills). Arunachal and Assam birds belong to IN-NORTHEAST: hornbills, wren-babblers, pittas, Blyth's Tragopan, Rufous-necked Hornbill and the like are not here. Birds that a Himalaya visitor also meets but that probably fit other packs were kept here on purpose and are for the owner to settle: Black Eagle, Pallas's Fish-Eagle, Asian Barred Owlet and Lesser Fish-Eagle were considered (the owlet and Lesser Fish-Eagle are left out), Orange-bellied Leafbird, Black-crested Bulbul, Black Bulbul, Silver-eared Mesia, Red-billed Leiothrix, Golden-throated Barbet, Darjeeling Woodpecker, Long-tailed Sibia, Beautiful Sibia, Black-faced and Rufous-necked Laughingthrushes. Not in the database for India, so not addable: Tibetan Snowfinch (tibsno2) and Blue Whistling-Thrush. Left out for lack of trustworthy photos in the library (reviewed from contact sheets): Hair-crested Drongo (hacdro1, photos dark and mixed with racket-tailed drongos), Hill Pigeon (hilpig1, sheet full of Rock Pigeon), Himalayan Cuckoo (himcuc1, cannot be told from Oriental Cuckoo), Buff-barred Warbler (bubwar1), Himalayan Prinia (strpri2), Robin Accentor (robacc1, only three poor shots), Alpine Thrush (alpthr1, look-alike thrushes mixed in), Grey-backed Shrike (gybshr1, mixed with Long-tailed and Brown Shrike). Add them back once reviewed photos exist. Shaky photo picks, to check on /trip-photos: Himalayan Snowcock and Tibetan Snowcock (distant, look-alike risk), Pallas's Fish-Eagle (mostly distant or immature), Golden Eagle (some immature, outside the Himalaya), Collared Owlet (mixed owlets), Snow Pigeon, Speckled Woodpigeon, Nepal House Martin, Eurasian Crag Martin, Pygmy Cupwing, Himalayan Flameback (flamebacks look alike), Slaty-headed Parakeet, Grey Treepie (sheet mostly Taiwan birds), Red-billed Blue-Magpie, Red-billed Chough, Long-tailed Minivet, Green-backed Tit, Rufous-vented Tit, White-tailed Nuthatch, Bar-tailed Treecreeper, Nepal Fulvetta, Chestnut-tailed Minla, Whiskered Yuhina, scimitar-babblers (Streak-breasted, White-browed), Black-chinned Babbler, Grey-hooded and Lemon-rumped Warbler, Ashy-throated Warbler, White-browed Tit-Warbler (quiz photos are non-males), Slaty-blue, Snowy-browed and Small Niltava, Large Niltava (some males may be Small Niltava), Plumbeous Redstart, Blue-capped Redstart (look-for line checked against photos by hand), Hodgson's Redstart (Daurian Redstart look-alike), White-bellied Redstart, Himalayan Bluetail, Himalayan Rubythroat, Blue-capped and Chestnut-bellied Rock Thrush (may be swapped), Grey Bushchat, Mistle Thrush, Slaty-backed Forktail (White-crowned Forktail look-alike), Plain Mountain Finch, Pink-browed and Dark-breasted Rosefinch, Twite, Black-winged Snowfinch, Tibetan Lark, Shore Lark (mostly non-Himalayan forms), Black-necked Crane and Crested Kingfisher (distant). Unverified facts in the shared look_for texts (written from memory, not confirmed on Wikipedia/eBird): Himalayan Rubythroat, Grandala, Dark-breasted, Himalayan Beautiful and Pink-browed Rosefinch, Great Rosefinch, Twite, plumage details of Black-headed Mountain Finch, Red-headed Bullfinch, Black-winged Snowfinch, Rufous-breasted Accentor, Tibetan Lark, Red-billed Leiothrix, Long-tailed Sibia, Rufous-vented Tit, White-cheeked Nuthatch, Bar-tailed Treecreeper, Pygmy Cupwing, Nepal Fulvetta, the crest and belly stripe of Himalayan Black-lored Tit and Green-backed Tit.
